panels.title: Service
panels.description: Is the scrape succeeding at all. Everything else on this dashboard is meaningless while this is DOWN.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Since the process started serving. A sawtooth here is a crash loop.

panels.title: Projects
panels.description: Projects in the database.

panels.title: Indexed files
panels.description: Files currently in the `indexed` state, across $project.

panels.title: Active chunks
panels.description: Chunks with a live vector — the searchable corpus.

panels.title: Failed files
panels.description: Files in `failed`. The retry worker is still trying, unless they also appear under 'Permanently failed' in GC & retry.

panels.title: SQLite DB
panels.description: page_count x page_size.

panels.title: In flight
panels.description: Requests being served right now. Long-lived /research streams live here for minutes by design.

panels.title: Request rate
panels.description: Total, client errors and server errors on one axis — they share a unit.

panels.title: Dependencies
panels.description: Sampled by the metrics collector on its own tick, off the request path — so this is availability over time, not a snapshot taken when someone happened to call /health. `query_embedder` appears only when the deployment is split.

panels.title: SQLite pool
panels.description: `available` riding at zero is the shape that precedes PoolEmpty. The counter below it is the confirmation.

panels.title: Pool exhaustion & claim conflicts
panels.description: Pool exhaustion is otherwise invisible — it collapses into an opaque 500. A claim conflict is two writers on one file; the request still succeeds for the rest of its batch.

panels.title: Concurrency
panels.description: The three in-process locks. `research_active` is derived from the semaphore rather than counted, because a run's normal exit is a dropped stream that no decrement would survive.

panels.title: Latency distribution
panels.description: The percentile lines hide bimodality; this does not.

panels.title: Error codes
panels.description: The stable machine `code` from the problem+json envelope, carried on the response extensions. `request.cancelled` at 499 is a client disconnect, not a fault.

panels.title: Transport
panels.description: Whether anyone actually reaches the HTTP/3 listener.

panels.title: In-flight by route
panels.description: A route stuck above zero with no traffic is a leaked gauge — which is exactly what the Drop guard exists to prevent.

panels.title: Files by outcome
panels.description: `skipped_unchanged` dominating is the hash skip working. `in_flight` is claim contention, not an error.

panels.title: Phase latency (p95)
panels.description: prepare = slice + insert; embed = the GPU pass; mark = the status writes. An embed phase that dwarfs the others is the normal shape.

panels.title: Submitted file size
panels.description: Language-labelled but never project-labelled — a histogram per project would multiply the series count for a breakdown nobody reads.

panels.title: Chunks per file
panels.description: A spike at the 1-2 bucket means files are slicing to almost nothing.

panels.title: Embed batch size
panels.description: Texts per /encode call. Indexing should cluster near `[indexing].embed_batch_chunks`; queries are always 1.

panels.title: Embed latency (p95)
panels.description: `index` and `query` are separate series even when one server does both — that is the split `[model].query_server_url` would create.

panels.title: Embedder 429 backoffs
panels.description: Counted inside the client: from outside, three retries then a success is indistinguishable from one success.

panels.title: Qdrant errors
panels.description: `delete_batch` errors here are the GC failures that keep chunk rows marked deleted for the next sweep — deliberately, since deleting the row first would orphan the vector forever.

panels.title: Searches by outcome
panels.description: `no_match` is an answer, not a failure — an empty candidate set returns 404 without ever calling Qdrant.

panels.title: Stage latency (p95)
panels.description: The two-SQL-queries-around-Qdrant shape, made visible: embed -> candidates -> qdrant -> fetch.

panels.title: Candidate set size
panels.description: The has_id filter lists every candidate GUID, so this grows linearly with a project's active-chunk count — the known scaling limit.

panels.title: Runs by stop reason
panels.description: The 'is a budget binding?' panel. `finalized` means the model judged the evidence sufficient; anything else is a wall it hit. Counted, not rated: one run per label set per process lifetime is invisible to `rate()`.

panels.title: Run duration
panels.description: One point per window that actually contained a run — with a few runs a day there is nothing to join into a line.

panels.title: Steps per run
panels.description: A step is a poor unit — one turn may execute several, and `outline` is one indexed SELECT while `search` is a GPU embed plus a vector query. That is why it is the backstop and not the budget.

panels.title: Turns per run
panels.description: Turns above steps means turns that produced no step: rejected duplicates, or a model rephrasing instead of learning a name.

panels.title: Context used
panels.description: Peak prompt tokens over the run's num_ctx. Approaching 1.0 means Ollama is about to trim the transcript in silence.

panels.title: Tokens processed
panels.description: The whole transcript is resent every turn, so prompt tokens grow super-linearly with turns. This is the real cost axis.

panels.title: Tool calls
panels.description: The intended path is list_files -> outline -> symbols/search/callers -> read_chunks. A run that only ever calls `search` never learned a name.

panels.title: Citations by provenance
panels.description: `unverified` = a path no tool returned this run, i.e. invented. `stale` is orthogonal to the other three: a citation can be impeccably verified and stale.

panels.title: Unverified citation share
panels.description: Over the dashboard's time range. A model that answers from its weights rather than from the index shows up here and nowhere else.

panels.title: Repairs & upstream faults
panels.description: A revalidation is a draft sent back because its citations did not check out. A truncation means Ollama trimmed the transcript and streamed on — otherwise a completely silent failure.

panels.title: Report length (words)
panels.description: Granted versus actual is the whole measurement: the per-effort max_report_words is announced to the model as a ceiling, and nothing makes it obey. If this sits wherever it likes regardless of the grant, the prompt half of that knob is dead weight and only num_predict earns its place.

panels.title: Report sections
panels.description: A report of 3+ plan items is written one section per turn, so one failing costs a section rather than the document. This says how often that trade is actually made. Rising `empty` means the per-section word budget or the model is wrong; `timed_out`/`skipped` mean report_timeout_ms is too tight for the plans being produced.

panels.title: Report-phase faults
panels.description: All three are expected to stay at zero. `generation cut off` means num_predict fired, so REPORT_WORDS_TO_TOKENS or the model is wrong and a cut landed mid-token — which can sever a fence and cost a rewrite. `prompt shed` means the report turn's transcript was over the context ceiling and the server dropped old tool output rather than letting Ollama trim it in silence; on this hardware it may never fire, in which case it is insurance. `server wrote the report` means the report window expired first — those runs cite nothing, which is why the citation panels beside this one must be read together with it.

panels.title: Stored research
panels.description: The corpus a new run can be given as context. `outdated` counts runs at least one of whose files has changed since — still useful for names, unreliable on specifics. `pinned` runs have no expiry and GC never reaps them, so a rising pinned count is the thing that stops retention from bounding this table.

panels.title: Context reuse
panels.description: Does prior research get reused, and does the character cap bite? Counted with increase() and drawn as bars: these are a handful of events a day, and a label set seeing one event in a process lifetime is flat at 1 under rate() forever.

panels.title: GC rows removed
panels.description: Only chunks whose Qdrant delete was confirmed are hard-deleted; the rest keep their rows for the next sweep.

panels.title: GC backlog
panels.description: Soft-deleted chunks whose vectors still sit in Qdrant. Indexing is append-only, so this rises on every reindex and falls on the hourly sweep. A monotonic rise means the sweep is failing.

panels.title: Retry outcomes
panels.description: `skipped_claim` dominating means the worker is racing live /index traffic, which is different from it failing.

panels.title: Permanently failed files
panels.description: Files that exhausted `[workers].max_retries`. The retry worker will never touch them again — they need a re-push. Until now this existed only as an hourly WARN.

panels.title: Projects
panels.description: Recomputed by the metrics collector every `[metrics].refresh_interval_seconds`, and cleared and repopulated each tick — so a deleted project disappears here rather than reporting its last known state forever.

panels.title: Files by language
panels.description: A bar rather than a pie: there are more than a handful of languages and their values are close, which is exactly where a pie stops being readable.

panels.title: Drift reported per check
panels.description: A counter, not a gauge: /drift compares against a manifest only the client can produce, so there is no server-side drift level. This is what the checks that ran reported.
